quickSummary: VBT explains covalent bonding through pairing of opposite-spin electrons in overlapping atomic orbitals. Sigma (σ) axial overlap is stronger than Pi (π) lateral overlap. Formal charge and resonance describe delocalized electron structures.
summary: Master VBT orbital overlaps, σ vs π bond mechanics, formal charge calculations, and resonance stabilization.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 4.1 Orbital Overlaps: Sigma (σ) vs Pi (π) Bonds
conceptBreakdown.title: 4.1 Orbital Overlaps: Sigma (σ) vs Pi (π) Bonds

summaryBox.title: Orbital Overlap
summaryBox.takeaway: σ-bond: Head-on axial overlap (s-s, s-p, p-p); π-bond: Lateral sideways overlap (p-p, p-d). Bond strength: σ(p-p) > σ(s-p) > σ(s-s) > π(p-p).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
ORBITAL OVERLAP TYPES
                                     │
         ┌───────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                       ▼
  SIGMA (σ) BOND                                          PI (π) BOND
  ├── Head-on / End-to-end axial overlap                  ├── Sideways / Lateral parallel overlap
  ├── Co-axial with internuclear axis                     ├── Perpendicular to internuclear axis
  ├── Cylindrically symmetric electron cloud              ├── Two electron lobes above/below axis
  └── Overlap: s-s, s-p_x, p_x-p_x                        └── Overlap: p_y-p_y, p_z-p_z, p-d, d-d
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Bond Strength Sequence**:
$$\mathbf{\sigma(p-p) > \sigma(s-p) > \sigma(s-s) > \pi(p-p)}$$
$p$-orbitals are directional, producing greater orbital overlap along the internuclear axis than spherical $s$-orbitals.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 4.2 Formal Charge (FC) & Resonance in Carbonate (CO3²⁻)
conceptBreakdown.title: 4.2 Formal Charge (FC) & Resonance in Carbonate (CO3²⁻)
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
RESONANCE IN CARBONATE ION (CO₃²⁻)
                        
   3 Equivalent Canonical Forms ──► Resonance Hybrid with fractional Bond Order (BO)
   
   BO = (Total bonds between two atoms across canonicals) / (Total resonating structures)
   BO = 4 / 3 = 1.33
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Formal Charge Formula**:
$$\mathbf{\text{FC} = V - N - \frac{B}{2}}$$
where $V$ is free atom valence electrons, $N$ is non-bonding lone pair electrons, and $B$ is total bonding electrons sharing the atom.

• **Resonance Energy**:
$$\mathbf{\text{Resonance Energy} = E_{\text{experimental (hybrid)}} - E_{\text{calculated (most stable canonical)}}}$$

quickRevision: σ-bond is stronger than π-bond due to axial overlap.
Bond strength: σ(p-p) > σ(s-p) > σ(s-s) > π(p-p).
Formal charge: FC = V - N - B/2.
Resonance hybrid of CO₃²⁻ has bond order BO = 4/3 = 1.33.
